Independent review of run r-20260926T162158829752-fenced-launch-resolves-the-backend (project reckon, plan a-worker-cannot-write-your-home section 2, source node fenced-launch-resolves-the-backend, source head 2435e6cb60562622a3da20e9019f6c58187d94b5, source base 4b6042ae8758f2fb521f010cd25d1aa2e2e93830). Read: the source manifest and its logs, the six-file diff commit by commit (d3898433, 7af45521, 9f779430, 2435e6cb), the three production call sites, and the plan and evidence records the change lands. No full suite was re-run; the two runs recorded here are the base arm the manifest claims and the single new test file the gate names.

The determination this review fence asks for, answered by the git diff and its output below. At head 2435e6cb the only change to tests/test_crew_launch_resolution.py is the argv position read by the two edited tests: a helper is added at :164 and the two reads switch to it at :190 and :219. The file's diff is exactly three hunks (16 changed lines by diff --stat), the file still carries the same six tests at both revisions, and every other assertion in that file is byte-identical to the base: the assertion-content check below exits 0 and prints ASSERTIONS-CONTENT-IDENTICAL, with only line numbers shifted by the twelve added helper lines.

Verbatim git diff 4b6042ae..2435e6cb -- tests/test_crew_launch_resolution.py

diff --git a/tests/test_crew_launch_resolution.py b/tests/test_crew_launch_resolution.py
index a7b524dc..027bd818 100644
--- a/tests/test_crew_launch_resolution.py
+++ b/tests/test_crew_launch_resolution.py
@@ -161,6 +161,18 @@ def _dispatch(
     return seen
 
 
+def _harness_executable(plan) -> str:
+    """The element of a launch plan the worker will actually run.
+
+    A fenced plan leads with the fence binary and carries the harness behind
+    that fence's own ``--`` separator; an unfenced plan's harness is its first
+    element. The position is read through the module's own helper, so this reads
+    the same element the resolution rewrites.
+    """
+    argv = list(plan.argv)
+    return str(argv[dispatch_module.harness_command_index(argv)])
+
+
 def test_a_dispatch_plan_carries_an_absolute_executable(
     project: tuple[Path, Path],
     tmp_path: Path,
@@ -175,7 +187,7 @@ def test_a_dispatch_plan_carries_an_absolute_executable(
 
     seen = _dispatch(repo, _config(_backend_environment(str(bin_dir))), monkeypatch)
 
-    executable = seen["plan"].argv[0]
+    executable = _harness_executable(seen["plan"])
     assert Path(executable).is_absolute()
     assert Path(executable) == fake.resolve()
     assert Path(executable).name == "codex"
@@ -204,7 +216,7 @@ def test_a_launcher_reached_through_a_symlink_keeps_its_own_name(
 
     seen = _dispatch(repo, _config(_backend_environment(str(bin_dir))), monkeypatch)
 
-    executable = Path(seen["plan"].argv[0])
+    executable = Path(_harness_executable(seen["plan"]))
     assert executable.is_absolute()
     assert executable == bin_dir / "codex"
     assert executable.name == "codex"

And the assertion-content check, whose output is the answer's evidence:

    diff <(git -C <worktree> show 4b6042ae:tests/test_crew_launch_resolution.py | grep 'assert ') \
         <(git -C <worktree> show 2435e6cb:tests/test_crew_launch_resolution.py | grep 'assert ')
    exit 0, no output, then: ASSERTIONS-CONTENT-IDENTICAL

The base defect, reproduced by this review at base 4b6042ae with the head revision's test file copied into a scratch tree: logs/reviewer-base-arm.txt records 4 failed, 2 passed in 6.29s, and the failure text is the defect itself — assert 'codex' in "backend command 'bwrap' cannot be resolved on the PATH this launch would search: /tmp/rv-base/reckon/host_shims:/nonexistent-backend-bin — install it or add its directory to PATH, then retry; nothing has been launched". The node's own new test file re-run at head: logs/reviewer-verify-head.txt records module /tmp/rv-head/reckon/crew/dispatch.py, cwd /tmp/rv-head, 3 passed, EXIT=0.

Out-of-scope observations, recorded here and in this review node's manifest follow_ons, not scored against the reviewed node:

- reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7170 (the lane-change record) still writes "command": str(target_plan.argv[0]), so a lane-changed fenced run records the fence binary as the command it ran. This is pre-existing (base:7080) and untouched by this diff; the read-time recovery through _names_the_fence / _harness_behind_the_fence covers it on the way back in.
- logs/gate-head.txt in the reviewed run's directory is a superseded mid-flight log whose header names revision 4b6042ae while its result (3 failed, 19 passed) is not a base-arm result — my own base arm reproduces 4 failed, 2 passed, matching the manifest's stated baseline. The manifest does not cite that log, but a later reader browsing the run directory could take it for the base arm.
